title: Best Peec AI Alternatives (2026): Honest Picks for AI Visibility Tracking
metaDescription: Peec AI alternatives compared fairly: pricing, engine coverage, free options, and which tool fits you — from a free instant audit to enterprise analytics.
shortAnswer: Peec AI is a strong AI-search visibility tracker, but people look for alternatives because it has no free plan (just a 7-day trial), its affordable tiers cover only 3 engines with extra models as paid add-ons, and it diagnoses gaps without telling you how to fix them. If you want to see your cross-engine visibility right now for free, start with AEOeye — it queries ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, Claude, and Gemini instantly with no sales call. For affordable paid monitoring choose Otterly AI; for enterprise analytics, Profound; and for combined SEO plus AI tracking, Nightwatch.
intro:
Peec AI does one thing well: it tracks whether AI engines mention and cite your brand, benchmarks you against competitors, and shows which sources the models pull from. It's a credible tool. But "credible" and "right for you" aren't the same thing, and most people searching for Peec AI alternatives hit one of three walls — the real cost once you add the engines and markets you need, the fact that it tells you what's broken without helping you fix it, or thin engine coverage on the plans most teams actually buy.

This page lays out those three reasons honestly, then walks through the best alternatives — starting with AEOeye, which lets you check your AI visibility for free in minutes, and including Otterly AI, Profound, and Nightwatch, each described fairly with where it genuinely wins.

sections.heading: Expensive once you add the engines and markets you actually need
sections.body:
The headline price isn't the price you pay. Peec's entry Starter tier (~€89-95/mo) covers ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews, with a 25-prompt quota that fills up fast if you track more than a handful of buyer questions. And there's no free plan to ease in — only a 7-day trial, so you commit before you've lived with the data for a full reporting cycle.

The add-ons are where budgets drift. Each extra model — Gemini, Claude, Grok, DeepSeek — is a paid add-on, commonly cited around €20-30 each per month, or roughly +$30/mo on Starter and +$70/mo on Pro per model. Extra countries are billed separately too. Stack two or three engines and a couple of markets and you're 30-50% over the advertised number.

For agencies this compounds per client. Reviewers describe a single new account adding $500+ in monthly tooling once you give it real engine and market coverage. None of this makes Peec overpriced for what it does — but if predictable, all-in pricing matters to you, it's a real reason to compare. Several alternatives below either include more engines at the base tier or, in AEOeye's case, let you start free.

sections.heading: Tells you what's wrong but not how to fix it
sections.body:
This is the single most repeated criticism of Peec AI across independent reviews, and it's fair: it's excellent at diagnosis and largely silent on treatment.

Peec will show you that you're invisible for a key prompt, that a competitor gets cited three times as often, and that ChatGPT keeps pulling from a Reddit thread and two review sites. That's genuinely useful visibility. What it won't give you is a recommendations engine, a content editor or brief generator, or a prioritized list of steps to actually close those gaps. There's no "do this next" layer.

For a data-literate in-house SEO or a GEO specialist who already knows how to act on a citation gap, that's fine — they want the raw signal and will build the playbook themselves. For a marketer who wants the tool to also point at the fix, it's a gap you'll feel weekly. Be honest with yourself about which you are. If you mainly need a fast, clear read on where you stand across engines, a lighter tool (or a free audit) may serve you better than paying for analytics depth you won't fully action.

sections.heading: Limited engine coverage on the plans most people buy
sections.body:
AI search isn't just ChatGPT anymore, but Peec's affordable tiers behave as if it mostly is. Out of the box the entry plans center on ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews — while Gemini, Claude, and Grok require paid add-ons.

That matters because those add-on engines are a growing share of how people actually research. Gemini ships in Google's ecosystem and Android; Claude has a fast-growing user base; Grok rides X. If a buyer asks Gemini "what's the best [your category]" and you're only tracking three engines, you're blind to that result until you upgrade. The cross-engine picture — the whole reason to buy an AI visibility tool — is gated behind extra spend on the tiers most teams can afford.

This is a fixable annoyance rather than a flaw: pay for the add-ons and the coverage is there, and Peec's per-engine analytics are well-built. But if seeing your full multi-engine footprint without an upgrade conversation is the point, tools that include more engines at the base level (Otterly AI's four, Nightwatch's four including Claude) or that query five engines for free (AEOeye) close that gap more directly.

sections.heading: AEOeye — free, instant, multi-engine (start here)
sections.body:
If your first question is simply "where do I actually stand across AI engines right now," AEOeye is the fastest way to answer it — and it's free to start, with no trial clock, no credit card, and no sales call.

AEOeye runs an instant AI visibility audit: it asks ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, Claude, and Gemini the real questions your buyers ask, then shows whether each engine recommends you, where you rank, and which competitors win the answer instead. It's a blind, multi-engine query across all five at once — the cross-engine view that costs extra elsewhere is the default here. It's also built for non-experts: you get a clear read in minutes, not a dashboard you need a specialist to interpret.

Be clear on the trade-off. AEOeye is newer and deliberately lighter on enterprise analytics, historical trend dashboards, and granular source-attribution depth than incumbents like Peec or Profound — its deeper multi-engine querying activates with continued use rather than out of a heavyweight setup. If you need years of historical benchmarking and procurement-grade reporting today, pair it with one of the platforms below. But for an honest, immediate, all-engine baseline at zero cost, it's the natural first move — run the audit, then decide what (if anything) to pay for.

sections.heading: Otterly AI — the affordable paid monitor
sections.body:
Otterly AI is the most natural like-for-like swap when Peec's pricing or trial-only model is the sticking point. Its Lite plan is $29/mo with 15 prompts, four AI engines, and 50+ country tracking, and there's a genuine 14-day free trial with no credit card — more room to evaluate than Peec's 7 days.

Where Otterly wins: a low entry price with four engines included rather than three plus add-ons, broad country coverage even on the cheap tier, and unlimited team members on every plan, which agencies appreciate. Standard ($189/mo, 100 prompts, daily tracking) and Premium ($489/mo, 400 prompts) scale up cleanly.

Where to be fair to Peec: some engines (notably Gemini and Google AI Mode) are still add-ons on Otterly too, and Peec's competitor benchmarking and source-tracking depth are well-regarded. Otterly, like Peec, is primarily a monitoring tool — it tells you where you stand more than how to fix it. Pick Otterly if you want straightforward, low-cost AI-search monitoring with a real free trial and more engines at the base tier; pick Peec if its specific competitor and source analytics are what you're after.

sections.heading: Profound — enterprise-grade analytics
sections.body:
If your reason for leaving Peec is that you want more depth and scale rather than less, Profound is the enterprise end of the market. It's a sales-led platform: Starter is around $99/mo (ChatGPT only), Growth $399/mo (three engines), and the all-engine, full-feature experience lives on custom Enterprise pricing.

What you get for that: standout features like Prompt Volumes (panel data on what real users are actually asking AI engines, with regional and demographic breakdowns), a Shopping module for product placement in ChatGPT Shopping, API access, SSO/SAML, SOC 2, and a dedicated account team. Profound raised a $96M Series C in early 2026 and works with large brands — it's built for procurement-heavy buyers who need serious coverage and support.

The honest trade-off versus Peec: Profound is materially more expensive and more enterprise-oriented, and its best intelligence (like Prompt Volumes) is gated to Enterprise. There's no instant free way in. Choose Profound if you're an enterprise or agency that needs broad market coverage, real user-prompt intelligence, and procurement-grade controls — and has the budget to match. For a smaller team, it's more platform than you need.

sections.heading: Nightwatch — SEO and AI visibility in one tool
sections.body:
Nightwatch is the pick if you don't want a separate subscription for AI visibility on top of your existing rank tracker. It's a mature SEO platform that added AI tracking, so you get traditional keyword rank tracking and AI-engine monitoring under one roof.

Pricing reflects that combo: SEO tracking starts around $32/mo (250 keywords), the AI Tracking add-on is about $99/mo (100 prompts), and the combined SEO-plus-AI setup lands near $131/mo. It tracks four AI models — ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews — with Claude included rather than as an extra, and adds citation-level sentiment analysis and prompt research. Every plan includes unlimited users and a 14-day free trial.

Where it's stronger than Peec: consolidation. If you're already paying for rank tracking, folding AI visibility into the same tool avoids tool sprawl, and the per-keyword (not per-seat) pricing is agency-friendly. Where Peec stays ahead: as a dedicated AI-search platform, Peec's competitor benchmarking and source attribution go deeper, and Nightwatch's four engines omit Gemini and Grok. Choose Nightwatch if you run both SEO and AI programs and want one bill; choose a dedicated tool if AI visibility is your whole focus.

keyTakeaways: Peec AI is a solid AI-visibility tracker, but the common reasons to seek alternatives are real cost creep from paid engine/market add-ons, diagnosis without fix recommendations, and only three engines on the affordable tiers.
Peec has no free plan — only a 7-day trial — and adding Gemini, Claude, or Grok plus extra countries can push the true cost 30-50% above the sticker price.
Start with AEOeye for a free, instant, blind audit across all five major engines (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, Claude, Gemini) — the cross-engine view that costs extra elsewhere is the default.
Be honest about AEOeye's limits: it's newer and lighter on enterprise analytics and historical dashboards than Peec or Profound, and its deeper querying activates with use.
For affordable paid monitoring with a real 14-day trial and four engines at the base tier, Otterly AI ($29/mo) is the closest like-for-like swap.
Pick Profound for enterprise-grade analytics and real user-prompt intelligence, and Nightwatch if you want SEO rank tracking and AI visibility consolidated into one bill.

faqs.q: Does Peec AI have a free plan?
faqs.a: No. Peec AI offers only a 7-day trial, not a free tier. If you want to check your AI visibility for free, AEOeye runs an instant audit across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, Claude, and Gemini with no credit card and no trial clock. Otterly AI and Nightwatch each offer a longer 14-day free trial on their paid plans if you want extended hands-on evaluation.

faqs.q: What's the cheapest Peec AI alternative?
faqs.a: For free, AEOeye lets you run a multi-engine AI visibility audit at no cost. For a paid, ongoing monitor, Otterly AI's Lite plan at $29/mo is the most affordable real alternative — it includes 15 prompts, four AI engines, and 50+ country tracking, with a 14-day free trial. Nightwatch's SEO tracking starts around $32/mo, but adding AI tracking pushes it to roughly $131/mo combined.

faqs.q: Which alternative covers the most AI engines without paid add-ons?
faqs.a: AEOeye queries five engines — ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, Claude, and Gemini — for free, with no add-on tiers. Among paid tools, Otterly AI and Nightwatch include four engines at the base level (Nightwatch notably includes Claude), versus Peec's three on its affordable tiers, where Gemini, Claude, and Grok are paid add-ons.

faqs.q: Will any of these tools tell me how to fix my AI visibility, not just measure it?
faqs.a: This is Peec's most cited limitation — it diagnoses without recommending fixes — and most monitoring tools (Otterly, and Peec itself) share that focus on measurement. AEOeye is built to make the gaps clear and act on, showing exactly which engines miss you and which competitors win, so non-experts can decide what to change. For deep content-optimization workflows, you'd typically pair any monitor with separate SEO/content tooling.

faqs.q: Is Profound better than Peec AI?
faqs.a: It depends on your scale. Profound is more enterprise-focused, with standout features like Prompt Volumes (real user-prompt panel data), a Shopping module, API access, and SOC 2 — but it's more expensive and sales-led, with all-engine coverage on custom Enterprise pricing. For a mid-market team, Peec is more accessible. For a large brand or agency needing broad coverage and procurement-grade controls, Profound is the stronger fit. Neither offers a free instant audit the way AEOeye does.
